page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3s.8xlarge belongs to the d3s big data instance family and operates on the KVM hypervisor. Compute is provided by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provisions 32 dedicated virtual CPUs and 128 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 4.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs integrated into this configuration, targeting computational and storage workloads directly on the CPU cores.

Storage capacity is the primary focal point of the ecs.d3s.8xlarge, which integrates 190696 GB of local hard disk drive storage directly on the host node. This massive bundled storage array allows processing pipelines to bypass the latency and bandwidth limits of network-attached block devices. To facilitate cluster communication and large-scale data synchronization, the instance is provisioned with a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, preventing data transmission bottlenecks during distributed jobs.

The reliance on mechanical HDD storage introduces a clear architectural tradeoff. While delivering advantageous cost efficiency for high-capacity sequential throughput and raw bulk data retention relative to solid-state alternatives, it offers lower random IOPS and higher read and write latencies. Consequently, transactional databases requiring rapid random lookups are not appropriate. The hardware profile is instead aligned with big data environments, including Apache Hadoop, HDFS nodes, Apache Spark pipelines, data warehousing, and high-volume batch log processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3s.8xlarge is a big data virtual server engineered for massive storage density and high-throughput analytical workloads. Running on the KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs via an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz alongside 128 GB of RAM, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution. A primary differentiator is the inclusion of 190696 GB of bundled local HDD storage, offering substantial bulk storage directly on physical host hardware. Complementing this capacity is a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, ensuring rapid internode communication across distributed clusters. Because it uses mechanical hard disk drives, it prioritizes sequential streaming over low-latency random input and output operations. The instance is suited for Apache Hadoop, HDFS storage nodes, distributed data analytics, and large-scale batch data processing.
